narrative.overview:
The page is a night-mode message thread, not a website that happens to mention chatting. A Bohol business owner's question sits in a cream bubble on the left; Claude's answer sits in a gold bubble on the right, set at headline size because in this world the answer *is* the headline. Prices are not a table but a pinned message. The testimonials section does not exist because testimonials do not exist; the closest thing is six labelled concept posts arriving as photos, the way an owner would actually receive them.

Everything follows from that one premise. Rhythm is turn-taking, not sectioning: each exchange is separated by a large turn gap and nothing else. Type splits by who is talking — Bricolage Grotesque for every voiced statement (the answer, the questions, the plan names, the prices) and the phone's own system sans for the connective prose, which keeps the page feeling native and light on the mid-range Android that carries most of this traffic. Colour is grammar, not decoration: cream means the owner, gold means Claude, navy is the room. The world is dense with small true details — timestamps, a "Seen" mark, a green dot, an "Add-ons" disclosure — and quiet everywhere else: no office photography, no icon triad, no gradient, no stock face. The one photograph of a person is the real one.
keyCharacteristics: Two-voice chat: cream bubbles left, gold bubbles right, navy ground.
The h1 lives inside a gold bubble, not above the thread.
One pinned bill carries every price; rows open in place.
A composer at the foot, with radio chips and three send targets, is the only conversion surface.
Motion is interaction feedback only; the opening exchange renders instantly.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cream is what the visitor says, gold is what Claude says, navy is the room. A colour never decorates — it attributes. If a new element cannot be assigned to a speaker, it is chrome and belongs in night or rail.

rules.name: The Gold Is Spoken Rule
rules.body: Gold appears as a bubble, a chip, a price, a tag, or a ring. It never fills a band, a section background, or a gradient; there is no gold wash anywhere on the page.

rules.name: The Mist Is Meta Rule
rules.body: Mist never carries a message. It is legal to use it only for status, timestamps, units, terms and helper text at 0.75–0.9375rem.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Bricolage carries anything with a voice or a number; the system sans carries everything that explains it. Never set a paragraph in the display face, and never set a headline, plan name, or price in the system sans.

rules.name: The Tightening Rule
rules.body: Display tracking is negative and grows tighter as the type grows (−0.01em at title, −0.035em at display). Never letter-space display type; the only positive tracking in the system is 0.02em on micro stamps.

rules.name: The 17px Floor Rule
rules.body: A spoken message is 1.0625rem (17px); the only smaller messages are the 0.9375rem secondary notes that qualify one. Metadata never goes below 0.75rem (12px). The page is read between customers on a phone.

rules.name: The Turn Rule
rules.body: Separation is a turn, never a section padding. Nothing gets a top border, a band, or a background change to mark a new section — only a gap.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Speech lives in 46rem. The shelf is the single sanctioned exception; do not widen another block to full bleed.

rules.name: The Pick-Up Rule
rules.body: If it cannot be picked up — a section, a headline, a divider — it gets no shadow. Tonal steps carry depth everywhere else.

rules.name: The Tail Rule
rules.body: 1.4rem corners with 0.4rem on the speaker's bottom corner, and a run of bubbles from one speaker keeps its tail only on the last. The photo bubble is the one object allowed a tail on both right corners: it is an album, not a line of speech.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: A button is a pill or a circle, never a rounded rectangle. Disclosures are the exception and open by chevron on a plain text row (the price rows, Add-ons), because they are part of the ledger, not actions.

dos: **Do** put every spoken line in a bubble with a speaker: cream left for the visitor, gold right for Claude, `ink` text on both.
**Do** keep the h1 inside the opening gold bubble and the free check-up line directly beneath it, before the chips.
**Do** keep every price inside the one pinned bill, `<details>` rows, Plan B open and tagged.
**Do** end the thread with the composer, whose submit opens Messenger or email with a prefilled message; the `<footer>` below it is identity only.
**Do** label concept work in the thread itself, in the same voice, and keep the real headshot and CD monogram as the only identity marks.
**Do** hold spoken messages at 1.0625rem (17px) and every control at ≥2.75rem (44px).
donts: **Don't** add a hero headline block, eyebrow, or kicker above the thread, or a light section, a gold band, or a gradient fill to break up the scroll — the first thing in the body is the visitor's question, and separation is a turn gap.
**Don't** rebuild the prices as a comparison table or three-column cards; the bill's rows are the pattern.
**Don't** add testimonials, client logos, star ratings, or follower counts; none exist, and the page never fakes them.
**Don't** set prose in Bricolage or a headline/price in the system sans.
**Don't** add a second animation or a scroll reveal; the opening exchange is the only authored motion, and it disappears under reduced-motion.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows, bevels, or inner glows; depth is the four navy steps plus a soft downward lift.
